summary: The harness emits image_gen prompt packets and validates resulting files, but generated-asset manifests do not structurally prove which generator run and candidate produced an accepted asset. Make real Codex/GPT image generation provenance a fail-closed, versioned manifest property and migrate the World Cup Hub integrated asset.
decisions: A generated asset is not accepted on prompt text and file hashes alone; it must identify the actual generator, generation run, and selected candidate.
Keep prompt-packet construction deterministic while making the Visual Asset Producer responsible for invoking the available image tool and recording its returned identity.
Migrate the existing World Cup Hub asset from its verified Codex generated_images path instead of inventing provenance.

gate_results.command: jq -e '.assets[] | select(.acquisition_mode == "generated" and .status == "integrated") | has("generator") and has("generation_run_id") and has("candidate_id")' projects/world-cup-hub/public/generated/design-system/manifest.json
gate_results.evidence: The integrated generated hero records hashes and an original Codex path but lacks explicit generator, generation_run_id, and candidate_id fields.
Current prompt and registry tests pass, confirming the missing producer identity is not covered by the existing validation contract.

risks: Provenance fields must come from a real tool result or a verifiable local generation path; user-authored arbitrary strings must not be treated as equivalent evidence.
Changing the asset schema without a migration path would invalidate existing accepted assets.
next_action: Visual Asset Producer adds versioned generator/run/candidate provenance validation and tests, updates the image-generation skill contract, migrates the verified World Cup Hub asset, validates all image assets, and returns a schema-valid handoff with current hashes.
